alt: Hiding in the noise: how an attacker can imitate natural noise on a satellite downlink, and why the testbed still catches it
The signal we chose: a fixed X-band carrier at 8477.8 MHz, moved only by Doppler, −88.8 to −74.4 dBm at Zaghouan
Natural noise has a signature: Gaussian thermal noise, and carrier, power and timing residuals inside a narrow envelope
Three ways to look like nature: noise-shaped jamming, fade-mimicking spoofing, bit flips disguised as bit errors
The physical layer: a jammer 5.3 dB below the thermal noise stays hidden, bounded to 1.1 dB of SNR, and every frame verifies
Push harder and the chi-square gate fires: the imitation becomes visible
The statistical layer: an Isolation Forest trained on clean passes reads what the chi-square cannot see
The data layer: noise cannot forge an HMAC-SHA256 tag; one failure is resent, two tiers at once quarantine the link
Result: every attack packet flagged, no corrupted frame reached the analyst, about 1.6% of genuine packets held for review
